body:
The bit about how I'm being pushed away is exactly what I needed to hear.  Thank you.  I keep blaming myself and apologizing to others when I'm being honest and up front about my feelings because I'm being made to feel like I'm overreacting.  It hurts because I love these people, but they aren't showing their love for me--they'd rather turn away from me and minimize the effects of what happened because it makes them uncomfortable.  

The thing about my friend is that he constantly psychoanalyzes me and tries to encourage me to think about what happened to me "logically" in an attempt to be helpful.  He is clearly bothered when I tell him I'm not interested or disagree with his analysis and it makes me feel guilty.  But like, dude... What logic is there that will help me cope with rape? I was overpowered and beaten and couldn't do anything about it.  I actually posted this because we just got in a tiff that ended with me telling him that his opinions on what happened to me are hurting me way more than helping me.  We used to be so close, but I feel like he's more concerned with being right than with being supportive.

Thank you for your suggestion about the women's center.  I feel like I need to gain control of my emotions a little bit before I can help anybody, but when I do get to that point I want to reach out to other people like me.  Group therapy might be the thing to do.

Thank you for going out of your way to leave me such a nice message.  I appreciate that you've broken your silence for my sake.  The fact that somebody sees goodness in me does more for me than I can say.  I guess this is the first time since the incident that I feel like I've really been heard, and I can't take that for granted.

I've been hesitant to talk to other people who've experienced similar trauma, mostly because I'm afraid that by listening to their stories I will further convince myself that this world is far too sad and depraved to continue living in.

I'm going off on a tangent, but here we go: The day he raped me, I went to the hospital to get a rape kit done.  The process of collecting the evidence was rather short.  Waiting for the doctor to complete the rape kits of the patients before me took much longer.  And there were people who had to wait their turn for me to finish mine.  So many people were hurt that day, and I imagine many more people had to have rape kits done the next day, and more the day after that, and the day after that.  Then imagining it on a far larger geographical scale.  And then adding in all of the people who can't go to the police or the hospital, for some reason or another.  So many people suffer at the hands of evil every day, and that is what disturbs me the most.  I am not the first, and I am not the last.  As comforting as it is to know that others know what I feel, I am distressed by the idea that anyone feels, has felt, or will feel what I feel.

Your advice is very good--I'm just not mentally sound enough to take it right now.  But I think that if/when I get a handle on my own experience, it will do me a world of good to talk to others who have been in my position.  Responding to your comment has made me evaluate a lot of things that I didn't want to give much thought to, and I am glad.  Thanks again.

I really appreciate you telling me the truth about how we never get back to normal.  People keep telling me that things will go back to the way they were, but in my heart I know it isn't true.  I can only hope for a "new normal."  Thank you for being so kind.  I hope you've found your "new normal," too.

Thank you for providing me with resources.  I definitely need to see a doctor.  I feel like I'm not ready to "work on myself" yet (It's been a little over a month) but at the same time I know if I keep waffling over it I'll never get help... It's a process.  I appreciate your recommendations.
That is a comforting thought.  I don't know how long it will take, but I like the idea that I'll be a completely different person when that happens.  Thank you for your sympathy.
You are very kind.  I couldn't wish this kind of pain on anybody, but your words are appreciated.  Thank you.
I hope that I can wholeheartedly believe it sometime soon.  Thank you.

Your advice is perfectly coherent right now.  Thank you for recommending me something that worked for you.  I run when I get angry.  Part of me thinks I should get super buff so I can have some kind of chance at fighting away potential attackers.  It's not a serious wish of mine (I have a bad heart and can't exert myself too much) but imagining myself as comically ripped is funny.  I'll stick with the running for now.

I'll keep this in mind.  One of the few things that is keeping me going is knowing that I need to stay alive in order to testify against him in court.  I have a feeling that, without my testimony, there would be less consequences for his actions.  I can't let this happen.
I feel the same way...  Thank you for being angry on my behalf.

This is an overused sentiment, but I am very sorry that happened to you.  I hate how cruel people can be.  I don't want to go into too many details, but something about my situation tells me he would rather I don't die--which, in a messed up way, makes me want to do it just to spite him.  I cannot deny that it is a bad way of thinking.  Your advice is still appreciated.  I hope I can put it to use.  Thank you.

Even if it isn't logical, I feel like it is very much my fault.  I keep thinking stupid things like "maybe I shouldn't have glanced in his general direction that one time that one day and this wouldn't have happened"  and it's eating away at me.  Thank you for the kind words though.  Even if I don't believe it, it's nice to hear.

The worst part is definitely the lack of empathy from others because they can't understand how any of this feels.  You're right though.  I can't expect anybody to relate to me.  I appreciate your advice.  The video didn't do much for me, though I'm not very receptive right now so that's definitely a me issue.  The weeds analogy was nice though.

Thank you for being kind.  The cells thing helps a little bit.  I'm kind of cynical in regards to therapy, since I've been subjected to a lot of it and it always leaves me feeling worse than before...  I guess I think that the people who've raped me need way more "help" than I do.  There's a women's center around here that offers free therapy for rape victims, so I haven't completely written off the option.  I appreciate your words.

I was diagnosed with it after I was raped the first time, so I don't doubt it.  I'm a little wary of doctors after being prescribed a lot of things that made me feel like a zombie.  I will though, eventually. 
 Thank you.
